text:
infra-bot: ALERT: High rate of serving runtime failures in eu-west GPU pool. Errors: CUDA OOM, container crashloop on model-serving v2. Rolling error rate spike at 09:12 UTC. Pager sent to @sre-rotation :rotating_light:

michael: ack, I'm on it. pulling logs now.

lucy: seeing ~30% 5xx on /v1/generate for redwood-prod-eu cluster, customers getting timeouts. dashboard: https://rwd.infra/d/serve/errors?env=prod-eu

michael: quick check: `kubectl get pods -n serve -l app=model-server -o wide` shows many restarts.

michael: tailing one pod log:
```
2026-03-15T09:13:02Z ERROR runtime: CUDA error: out of memory
2026-03-15T09:13:02Z INFO restarting process: exitcode=137
```

tara: that looks like autoscaler thrash — nodes are being added then immediately pods hit OOM and crash, causing more scale events. we saw similar with the new burst policy last week.

michael: confirmed: HPA events show scale from 6 -> 18 in 2m, then node eviction, then pods crash, then cluster autoscaler removes nodes.

sre-rotation: @michael @tara take it. i'm happy to help with comms.

michael: plan: 1) pause autoscaler burst policy 2) pin model v2 -> v2-slim variant on eu region via routing policy 3) increase pod nodeSelector to use larger-gpu nodes 4) add damping to autoscaler (cooldown 5m). executing now.

michael: pausing burst: `kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -n infra -p '{"data":{"burst_enabled":"false"}}'` -> applied.

lucy: routing change to fallback variant: updating route table. `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/routes -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"v2-slim","region":"eu"}'` -> 200.

michael: scaling policy change: set cluster-autoscaler `--scale-down-delay=300s` and `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` via deployment rollout. `kubectl apply -f ca-patch.yaml` -> rollout started.

deploy-bot: deploy infra/cluster-autoscaler patch started (deployment/cluster-autoscaler) — rollout 1/2 replicas ready.

lucy: manually cordoned two hotspot nodes that repeatedly OOM'd to stop churning: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-23` and `node-gpu-27`.

tara: restarting crashlooping pods with pinned memory limits: applying resource patch to model-server: `resources: requests: cpu: 2, memory: 24Gi` -> applied.

michael: monitoring. error rate dropping but still occasional OOMs. will increase per-pod memory limit if needed.

sre-rotation: handoff @tara -> i'm off shift in 20. if you need me to stay, tell me now.

tara: i'm taking on-call. @michael can you summarize customer impact for comms?

michael: impact: approx 12 customer sessions experienced 5xx during 09:11-09:25 UTC, primarily EU region. no data loss; requests retried by our client SDKs. we've sent CS a short note.

customer-succ: notified affected customers with templated message, pushing ETA 30m for full stabilization.

lucy: infra metrics now: pod restart rate down 80%, GPU mem utilization trending lower after route switch.

michael: still seeing one pod in CrashLoopBackOff on node-gpu-31. digging deeper — looks like mixed-precision kernel selection causing spike on longer sequences. adding kernel fallback flag to runtime: `--force-fp32-fallback=true`.

tara: go for it. small risk to latency but better than brownout.

michael: applied runtime flag via configmap update and restarted runtime DaemonSet. `kubectl rollout restart ds/serve-runtime` -> restart triggered.

infra-bot: NOTE: configuration change made by michael: runtime fp32 fallback enabled.

lucy: after runtime change, CrashLoopBackOff cleared on node-gpu-31, restarts stopped. error rate back to baseline.

tara: great. next steps: 1) keep autoscaler burst disabled for 1h 2) telemetry team to collect traces for sequence length distribution 3) infra to schedule longer-term change: adjust burst policy or set max surge lower.

michael: filing post-incident ticket with timeline, root cause hypothesis (burst + kernel selection on long seqs -> transient OOMs) and mitigation steps. assigning to eng-runtime and autoscale teams.

sre-rotation: thanks team. i'm handing off to tara for continued watch. I'll update rotations.

tara: I'm on watch. if we see re-escalation ping me. otherwise i'll merge incident doc and run retrospective tomorrow. :white_check_mark:

michael: incident resolved -> moving to monitoring state. closing pager. :thumbsup:
